Q: Which browsers do support MathML? A:

Almost none, only Firefox and Safari can handle MathML.

See https://caniuse.com/mathml

But there is a workaround available that replaces the unsupported MathML formulas by HTML and CSS: MathJax.js

Simply put the JavaScript file into your web page and your page will show correctly on almost all browsers. On Firefox this is basically a no-op.

<script type="text/javascript" src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/mathjax/2.7.2/MathJax.js?config=MML_HTMLorMML">

Once you have done that you might think about switching back to TeX instead of MathML. This is supported by MathJax as well. TeX is older, shorter and functional superior to MathML, and well, similarly unreadable for humans.

In this case the script include should be

<script type="text/javascript" src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/mathjax/2.7.2/MathJax.js?config=TeX-AMS_CHTML">

Q: Using Node.js, Ctrl + C doesn't the stop server (after starting the server with "npm start") A:

I had the same problem working with npm. But finally, I knew it was a problem with Git itself.

There was a comment by dscho on GitHub 15 days ago. He said that they're working to fix this problem in the next release. He also shared the exact msys-2.0.dll file that can fix the problem for the people who can't wait.

Personally, I couldn't wait :p. So, I gave it a try, downloaded the file, and throw it in the Git folder as he said. And the problem is gone! It was awesome!

But please be sure to take a backup before you replace the file.

I also tried to kill it after running express as I used to; using taskkill /im node.exe on the cmd, but there wasn’t any process to be found.

Check out this issue on GitHub, and search for the name of the file msys-2.0.dll to get to the comment faster.

Q: How should an early-stage Gmail client choose OAuth flow to pass verification without premature CASA costs? A:

A few things worth separating, because the cost picture changes a lot based on which scopes you actually need.

Sensitive vs restricted scopes — different verification paths

  • gmail.send and gmail.compose are sensitive scopes. Brand + sensitive scope verification only. No CASA.
  • gmail.modify, gmail.readonly, gmail.metadata, and the full gmail scope are restricted. These trigger CASA: Tier 2 self-assessment (free) or Tier 3 third-party Letter of Assessment (the $15k–$75k one).
  • Tier 3 only kicks in for apps that transfer restricted-scope data to a remote server. A pure client-side flow that never sends Gmail content to your backend can often stay in Tier 2.

If you can ship the first version with just gmail.send, you skip CASA entirely while you validate. Add gmail.modify later.

The "secure OAuth flows / impersonation" warning is a recommendation, not a verification blocker

It surfaces when your client is a public client (no client secret) — the correct setup for an SPA using GIS. Reviewers don't reject apps for verification on this basis; the warning is aimed at apps that should be confidential clients but aren't.

The bigger thing to know about GIS Token Client in the browser is that you only get access tokens, not refresh tokens. They expire in ~1 hour, so users hit a re-prompt that often unless you stand up a backend specifically to hold a refresh token issued via the auth-code flow. That's usually the real reason teams move to backend OAuth, not the verification posture.

Phased path reviewers typically accept

  1. Testing mode with up to 100 manually added users — no verification needed.
  2. Submit brand + sensitive scope verification for gmail.send only. Expect weeks, not days, and budget for back-and-forth on the demo video.
  3. Add gmail.modify and submit for restricted scope verification once you have validation. Self-assess for CASA Tier 2; only pay for Tier 3 if your architecture forces restricted-scope data into your backend.

Minimum implementation to keep verification posture strong

  • Refresh tokens encrypted at rest with a managed KMS.
  • Tokens never leave server memory in plaintext; logs scrub them.
  • Documented retention/deletion policy in your privacy policy.
  • TLS 1.2+ end-to-end, audit log of token reads/writes.

That's the substance of what reviewers want in the security questionnaire. SOC 2 isn't required for verification but it shortcuts a lot of the questions.

Q: How to set the default "line" color in the legend of a plot using title lc variable A:

gnuplot creates for one plot command line (if it's not a loop) one entry into the key/legend. So, if you have variable color, what color should gnuplot put into the legend? The first, the last or some color inbetween? I am not aware that you can set some "default color". You need to set it up differently.

You could plot your data (as it seem to work in your script) and do the legend manually. Check help keyentry. However, I assume you want to read the color values from the datafile.

As I understand you have data and want to filter and color the data based on 3 different columns. The script below creates some simplified test data.

# 1   2   3        4        5       6
# x   y   param1   param2   gender  color
  ...
  ...

Column 1,2:  x,y real values in the range [0:1]
Column 3:    parameter1 integer in the range [1:2]
Column 4:    parameter2 integer in the range [1:3]
Column 5:    gender integer in the range [0:1]
Column 6:    color integer in the range [1:3]

If you do a nested loop you can filter the data and set a fixed color in each iteration and set the entry in the legend accordingly. In the example below you can set your own colorsequence and the colors are shifted by 3 if column(5) is not 0 but 1. I hope you can adapt this minimal example to your needs.

Script:

### filter and color data according to 3 columns
reset session

# create some random test data
set table $Data
    plot '+' u (rand(0)):(rand(0)):(int(rand(0)*2+1)):(int(rand(0)*3+1)):(int(rand(0)*2)) w table
unset table

set key out noautotitle reverse Left

gender(g)  = word("male female",g+1)
colors     = "0xff0000 0x00ff00 0x0000ff 0xff00ff 0xffff00 0x00ffff"
color(c,g) = int(word(colors, int(column(c) + column(g)*3)))

plot for [p1=1:1] for [p2=1:3] for [g=0:1] $Data u 1: \
     ($3==p1 && $4==p2 && $5==g ? $2 : NaN):(color(4,5)) \
     w p pt 7 ps 2 lc rgb var ti sprintf("p%d%d, %s",p1,p2,gender(g))
### end script
